order.why_here: The decision tree itself: choose/explore/un-choose with one shared path, every node an answer.
Same tree with duplicate inputs: sort, then skip equal siblings to cut identical subtrees.
Switch from pick-from-index to pick-from-set: a used array replaces the start index.
First real prune: a remaining budget cuts subtrees, and recursing on i allows reuse.
Combines the budget break with the duplicate skip; i+1 because each index is used once.
Fixed-depth product with a different alphabet per level: recursion as variable nested loops.
Choices gated by counters so every branch is a prefix of a valid answer: pruning with zero dead ends.
Backtracking moves onto a grid: the used set becomes an in-place mark erased on the way back.
Grid walk that must cover every free cell: a remaining-cells count is both prune and success test.
Placement under conflicts: row-by-row choices with column and diagonal sets.
Constraint backtracking with bitmasks and most-constrained-cell-first to keep the tree narrow.
Search over deletions with a precomputed removal budget and balance pruning.
Carry running value plus last operand so multiplication precedence can be undone in O(1).
The state is a shrinking multiset: combine two values, recurse on the rest, with float tolerance.
Blind backtracking: the tree is unseen, and un-choose is a physical turn-around and step back.
